recipe.title: Raspberry-Lemon Protein Pancakes with Skyr and Pistachios
recipe.description: Light, tender lemon protein pancakes made with egg whites and skyr, served with fresh raspberries, cool skyr, maple syrup and crunchy pistachios.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use 50 g; standard plain wheat flour is suitable.
Use 200 g; carton size may vary.

ingredients.notes: Whole eggs do not scale perfectly for every serving quantity; round sensibly when scaling.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use 240 g; retail pot size may vary.
ingredients.notes: Use 60 g in the pancake batter and reserve 180 g for serving.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use 140 g; punnet size may vary.
ingredients.preparation: Inspect and rinse gently if required, then dry thoroughly.
ingredients.notes: Frozen raspberries are less suitable here because the fresh fruit provides useful cool texture and avoids excess moisture.

ingredients.preparation: Wash and dry before zesting and juicing.
ingredients.notes: Use finely grated zest in the batter and juice to sharpen the serving skyr.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use 16 g; retail pack size may vary.

ingredients.notes: A small amount balances the lemon and raspberries without making the breakfast excessively sweet.

ingredients.purchase_notes: Use up to 1 tsp across both pancake batches.

equipment.notes: A broad pan allows several small pancakes to cook in one batch.
Use for turning the pancakes cleanly.

mise_en_place.instruction: Finely grate the zest from approximately half of the lemon. Halve the lemon and squeeze the juice. Stir approximately 1 tsp lemon juice into 180 g of the skyr reserved for serving; keep the remaining juice available for final adjustment.
mise_en_place.endpoint: The serving skyr is smooth with a clean lemon acidity but remains thick enough to spoon.

mise_en_place.instruction: Roughly chop the pistachios. Inspect the raspberries, rinse gently if necessary and dry thoroughly so they do not water down the finished pancakes.
mise_en_place.endpoint: The pistachios are in coarse crunchy pieces and the raspberries are clean and dry.

mise_en_place.instruction: Measure 50 g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder and 1/8 tsp fine salt into the mixing bowl and whisk briefly to distribute the raising agent evenly.
mise_en_place.endpoint: The dry ingredients are evenly combined with no visible pockets of baking powder.

procedure.title: Mix the pancake batter
procedure.instruction: Add 200 g liquid egg whites, 1 medium egg, the remaining 60 g skyr, 1 tsp vanilla extract and the prepared lemon zest to the dry ingredients. Whisk just until the batter is smooth and no dry flour remains. Do not continue whisking once combined.
procedure.endpoint: The batter is smooth, thick but pourable, and falls from the whisk in a broad ribbon.

corrective_actions.condition: The batter is so thick that it does not spread at all when spooned.
corrective_actions.action: Mix in 1 tsp lemon juice or cold water, then reassess before adding more.

corrective_actions.condition: The batter appears thin and watery.
corrective_actions.action: Leave it undisturbed for 2 minutes so the flour hydrates before deciding whether any correction is needed.

procedure.title: Heat the pan
procedure.instruction: Place the frying pan over medium heat for approximately 1-2 minutes. Add approximately 1/2 tsp rapeseed oil and spread it into a very thin film over the cooking surface.
procedure.endpoint: The pan is evenly hot and the oil flows readily across the surface without smoking.

corrective_actions.action: Remove the pan from the heat for approximately 30 seconds and reduce the burner before adding batter.

procedure.title: Cook the first batch
procedure.instruction: Spoon 3 small pancakes into the pan, using approximately one-sixth of the batter for each. Leave space between them. Cook over medium heat for approximately 2-3 minutes, until the edges look set, the upper surfaces show bubbles and the undersides are evenly golden. Turn once and cook for a further 1-2 minutes, until the second side is golden and the centres are just set.
procedure.endpoint: The pancakes are golden on both sides, spring lightly when pressed and have no wet batter visible at the centre.

corrective_actions.condition: The undersides darken before bubbles appear and the edges set.
corrective_actions.action: Reduce the heat before continuing; the pan is too hot.

corrective_actions.condition: The pancakes remain pale after 3 minutes and spread excessively.
corrective_actions.action: Increase the heat slightly and allow the pan to recover before turning.
Wait another 30-45 seconds until the upper surface is more firmly set before trying again.

procedure.title: Cook the second batch
procedure.instruction: Add the remaining rapeseed oil only if the pan surface is dry. Cook the remaining batter as 3 pancakes using the same method and endpoint as the first batch.
procedure.endpoint: All 6 pancakes are evenly golden, tender and fully set through the centre without becoming dry.

corrective_actions.condition: The second batch colours more rapidly than the first.
corrective_actions.action: Reduce the heat slightly because the pan has accumulated additional heat.

procedure.title: Balance the lemon skyr
procedure.instruction: Taste the lemon skyr. If it needs more brightness, stir in up to another 1 tsp lemon juice. Keep the texture thick enough to sit on the pancakes rather than run off them.
procedure.endpoint: The skyr tastes distinctly lemony and fresh without becoming sharply sour or watery.

plating.instruction: Place 3 warm pancakes on each plate. Spoon half of the lemon skyr alongside or over each stack, divide the raspberries and chopped pistachios evenly between the plates, then drizzle each serving with half of the 1 tbsp maple syrup. Serve immediately so the pancakes remain warm against the cool skyr and raspberries.

storage.storage_instructions: Cool leftover pancakes promptly and refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 2 days, keeping the skyr, raspberries, pistachios and maple syrup separate. Pancakes may be frozen with parchment between layers for up to 1 month. Refrigerate opened skyr according to its package instructions.
reheating_methods: Toaster: reheat chilled pancakes briefly on a moderate setting until hot throughout, checking early to prevent excessive browning.
Frying pan: warm over low-medium heat for approximately 1-2 minutes per side until hot throughout.
Air fryer: heat at approximately 160°C for a few minutes until hot, checking frequently because the pancakes can dry quickly.

either_retailer: Liquid egg whites — 1 carton; use 200 g.
Unsalted shelled pistachios — 1 pack; use 16 g.
Pure maple syrup — 1 bottle; use 1 tbsp.
Rapeseed oil — use up to 1 tsp.

restaurant_quality_features: Fresh lemon zest perfumes the pancake batter without adding unnecessary sweetness.
Egg whites and skyr provide high protein while retaining a tender pancake texture.
Golden pan browning gives the pancakes savoury depth and crisp-edged contrast.
Cool lemon skyr contrasts with the warm pancakes.
Fresh raspberries provide sharp fruit acidity while pistachios add crunch and richness.
A restrained maple drizzle balances the lemon and berries without overwhelming them.
nutrition_notes: Approximately 385 kcal and 32 g protein per serving.
Skyr, egg whites and egg supply the majority of the protein without requiring protein powder.
Raspberries provide fruit, fibre and vitamin C.
Pistachios contribute unsaturated fats, minerals and textural contrast.
Nutrition values are estimates and will vary slightly with the exact skyr and egg-white products used.
critical_success_factors: Do not overmix the batter once the flour is hydrated.
Use medium rather than high heat so the relatively high-protein batter cooks through before the exterior becomes too dark.
Wait for set edges and visible bubbles before turning each pancake.
Keep the serving skyr thick and sharply lemony rather than thinning it excessively with juice.
Serve promptly to preserve the warm-pancake, cool-skyr contrast.
